P nonnegative for r²>=5 gives a forward radial bound; explicit variation of constants bounds z, hence global flow. The exact reciprocal-radius multiplier B=1/r has divergence [((15625mu-1764)/1764)-4mu(r²-125/84)²]/r, strictly negative a.e. on r>0 for mu<=1764/15625, excluding every periodic orbit and closed saddle separatrix via Green/Bendixson-Dulac. Reduced equilibria (r,z)=(1,-1/10) saddle, (2,-2/5) sink and (0,0) origin sink; bounded planar Poincare–Bendixson with unique saddle excludes other omega limit configurations. Hyperbolic convergence makes phase drift integrable; exact d/dt(theta+e z)=1 gives asymptotic phase. By Poincare recurrence every invariant Borel probability is carried on origin and two circles, and the saddle circle has a zero-volume stable manifold, giving exactly two physical ergodic measures. For general r^alpha multiplier, alpha<-1 gives divergence positive as |z|->infinity and for alpha>=-1 the minimized bracket is strictly decreasing in alpha, proving optimality at alpha=-1. Independent exact symbolic divergence, quadratic completion and Jacobian reconstructed; all orbits theorem uses actual topological proof, not finite simulation.
